scanNote:
GRAMMAR REFERENCE, 4-BET (119-bet). Yuqorida o'ngda 'Grammar Reference'.

CHAP USTUN (Qiyoslash davomi):
'Form': • One-syllable adjectives add -(e)r/-(e)st to form their comparative and superlative forms. 'cheap - cheaper (than) - the cheapest (of/in), large - larger (than) - the largest (of/in)' • Two-syllable adjectives ending in -ly, -y, -w also add -er/-est. 'heavy - heavier (than) - the heaviest (of/in)' • Adjectives of two or more syllables take more/most. 'expensive - more expensive (than) - the most expensive (of/in)' • Adverbs having the same form as their adjectives add -er/-est. 'fast - faster (than) - the fastest (of/in)' • Two-syllable or compound adverbs take more/most. 'quickly - more quickly (than) - the most quickly (of/in)'
'Spelling': • One-syllable adjectives ending in a vowel + a consonant double the consonant. 'fat - fatter (than) - the fattest (of/in)' • Two-syllable adjectives ending in a consonant + y replace -y with -ie. 'noisy - noisier (than) - the noisiest (of/in)'
'Use': • We use the comparative form to compare two people, things, places etc. We usually use than with comparative adjectives. 'The city is noisier than the country.' • We use the superlative form to compare one person or thing with more than one person or thing in the same group. We use the ... of/in with superlative adjectives. 'The giraffe is the tallest animal of all. He is the shortest student in the class.' • We can also use (not) as + adjective + as to say that two people, places or things are/are not similar. 'My brother is as tall as my father.' • We use much + comparative form. 'An elephant is much heavier than a mouse.'

O'NG USTUN:
To'q sariq 'UNIT 4'. 'PAST CONTINUOUS'. 'Form': We form the past continuous with was/were (past tense of the verb "to be") and add -ing to the base form of the main verb. OCh SARIQ QUTI: Affirmative: I was eating, you were eating, he was eating etc. Negative: I wasn't eating, you weren't eating, he wasn't eating etc. Interrogative: Was I eating?, Were you eating?, Was he eating? etc. Short answers: Yes, I/he/she/it was. Yes, you/we/they were. No, I/he/she/it wasn't. No, you/we/they weren't.
'Use': We use the past continuous for: • two or more actions happening at the same time in the past. 'John was cutting the grass while Jenny was planting flowers.' • an action which was in progress when another action interrupted it. We use the past continuous for the action in progress (longer action) and the past simple for the action that interrupted it. (shorter action). 'She was having a bath when the phone rang.' • an action in progress at a stated time in the past. 'James was sleeping at 9 o'clock last night.' • background information in a story. 'The wind was blowing when Jane left work last Friday.'
'ADVERBS': 'Adverbs usually describe verbs. He drives fast.' 'Form': • We usually form adverbs by adding -ly to the adjective. 'careful - carefully' • When the adjective ends with a consonant + y, we drop -y and add -ily to form the adverb. 'lucky - luckily' • Some adverbs have the same form as their adjectives. 'hard → hard, fast → fast, early → early' 'Note: good → well'

Bet raqami: pastda o'ngda '119'.

exercises.instructionEn: Form and spelling of comparatives and superlatives.
exercises.instructionUz: Qiyosiy va orttirma darajalarning shakli va imlosi.
exercises.explanationUz:
QIYoSLASh - ShAKLI:

  1 BIR BO'G'INLI → -(e)r / -(e)st:
    cheap - cheaper - the cheapest
    large - larger - the largest
  2 IKKI BO'G'INLI -ly, -y, -w →
    -er / -est:
    heavy - heavier - the heaviest
    narrow - narrower - the
    narrowest
  3 IKKI+ BO'G'INLI → more / most:
    expensive - more expensive -
    the most expensive
  4 SIFAT bilan bir xil RAVIShLAR →
    -er / -est:
    fast - faster - the fastest
  5 -LY RAVIShLAR → more / most:
    quickly - more quickly - the
    most quickly


IMLO:
  unli + undosh → IKKILANADI:
    fat - faTTer - the faTTest
    big - bigger, hot - hotter
  undosh + y → -IER / -IEST:
    noisy - noisier - the noisiest


⚠ 'THAN' / 'OF' / 'IN':

  cheaper THAN = ...dan arzonroq
  the cheapest OF all / IN the
  shop = hammasidan / do'kondagi
  eng arzon


⚠ 'COMPOUND':

  = qo'shma.

points.en: One-syllable adjectives add -(e)r/-(e)st. cheap - cheaper (than) - the cheapest (of/in), large - larger - the largest
points.uz: Bir bo'g'inli sifatlar -(e)r/-(e)st qo'shadi. cheap - cheaper (than) - the cheapest (of/in), large - larger - the largest

points.en: Two-syllable adjectives ending in -ly, -y, -w also add -er/-est. heavy - heavier (than) - the heaviest (of/in)
points.uz: -ly, -y, -w bilan tugagan ikki bo'g'inli sifatlar ham -er/-est qo'shadi. heavy - heavier (than) - the heaviest (of/in)

points.en: Adjectives of two or more syllables take more/most. expensive - more expensive (than) - the most expensive (of/in)
points.uz: Ikki va undan ko'p bo'g'inli sifatlar more/most oladi. expensive - more expensive (than) - the most expensive (of/in)

points.en: Adverbs having the same form as their adjectives add -er/-est. fast - faster - the fastest. Two-syllable or compound adverbs take more/most. quickly - more quickly - the most quickly
points.uz: Sifati bilan bir xil shakldagi ravishlar -er/-est qo'shadi. fast - faster - the fastest. Ikki bo'g'inli yoki qo'shma ravishlar more/most oladi. quickly - more quickly - the most quickly

points.en: Spelling: One-syllable adjectives ending in a vowel + a consonant double the consonant. fat - fatter - the fattest. Two-syllable adjectives ending in a consonant + y replace -y with -ie. noisy - noisier - the noisiest
points.uz: Imlo: unli + undosh bilan tugagan bir bo'g'inli sifatlar undoshni ikkilantiradi. fat - fatter - the fattest. Undosh + y bilan tugagan ikki bo'g'inli sifatlar -y ni -ie ga almashtiradi. noisy - noisier - the noisiest

exercises.instructionEn: Use of comparatives and superlatives. (not) as + adjective + as. much + comparative.
exercises.instructionUz: Qiyosiy va orttirma darajalarning ishlatilishi. (not) as + sifat + as. much + qiyosiy daraja.
exercises.explanationUz:
QIYoSLASh - IShLATILIShI:

  1 QIYoSIY DARAJA - IKKI narsani
    solishtirish, 'THAN' bilan:
    'The city is noisier THAN the
     country.'

  2 ORTTIRMA DARAJA - bittasini
    GURUH bilan solishtirish, 'THE
    ... OF/IN' bilan:
    'The giraffe is THE tallest
     animal OF all.'
    'He is THE shortest student IN
     the class.'

  3 (NOT) AS ... AS - bir xil / bir
    xil emas:
    'My brother is AS tall AS my
     father.' (bir xil bo'y)
    'He is NOT AS tall AS me.'
    (pastroq)

  4 MUCH + QIYoSIY - katta farq:
    'An elephant is MUCH heavier
     than a mouse.'
    ⚠ 'very heavier' - XATO!


⚠ 'SIMILAR':

  = o'xshash.


⚠ 'THE COUNTRY':

  bu yerda = qishloq joyi (shahar
  emas).

points.en: We use the comparative form to compare two people, things, places etc. We usually use than with comparative adjectives. The city is noisier than the country.
points.uz: Qiyosiy darajani ikki odam, narsa, joyni solishtirish uchun ishlatamiz. Qiyosiy sifatlar bilan odatda 'than' ishlatamiz. Shahar qishloqdan shovqinliroq.

points.en: We use the superlative form to compare one person or thing with more than one person or thing in the same group. We use the ... of/in with superlative adjectives. The giraffe is the tallest animal of all. He is the shortest student in the class.
points.uz: Orttirma darajani bir odam yoki narsani bir guruhdagi ko'pchilik bilan solishtirish uchun ishlatamiz. Orttirma sifatlar bilan 'the ... of/in' ishlatamiz. Jirafa hammasidan eng baland hayvon. U sinfdagi eng past bo'yli o'quvchi.

points.en: We can also use (not) as + adjective + as to say that two people, places or things are/are not similar. My brother is as tall as my father.
points.uz: Ikki odam, joy yoki narsa o'xshash/o'xshash emasligini aytish uchun (not) as + sifat + as ham ishlatishimiz mumkin. Akam otam bilan bir xil bo'yda.

points.en: We use much + comparative form. An elephant is much heavier than a mouse.
points.uz: Much + qiyosiy daraja ishlatamiz. Fil sichqondan ancha og'irroq.

exercises.instructionEn: Past Continuous. We form the past continuous with was/were and add -ing to the base form of the main verb. Affirmative: I was eating. Negative: I wasn't eating. Interrogative: Was I eating? Short answers: Yes, I was. / No, I wasn't.
exercises.instructionUz: O'tgan davomli zamon. O'tgan davomli zamonni was/were va asosiy fe'lga -ing qo'shib yasaymiz. Tasdiq: I was eating. Inkor: I wasn't eating. So'roq: Was I eating? Qisqa javoblar: Yes, I was. / No, I wasn't.
exercises.explanationUz:
PAST CONTINUOUS - ShAKLI.

  WAS / WERE + FE'L-ING

  TASDIQ: I/he/she/it WAS eating;
    you/we/they WERE eating
  INKOR: wasn't / weren't eating
  SO'ROQ: Was I eating? Were you
    eating?
  QISQA: Yes, I was. / No, I
    wasn't. Yes, they were. / No,
    they weren't.


PAST CONTINUOUS - IShLATILIShI:

  1 O'tmishda BIR VAQTDA bo'lgan
    ikki+ ish ('while'):
    'John WAS CUTTING the grass
     WHILE Jenny WAS PLANTING
     flowers.'

  2 DAVOM ETAYoTGAN ish UZILGANDA
    ('when'):
    uzun ish → past continuous
    qisqa ish → past simple
    'She WAS HAVING a bath WHEN the
     phone RANG.'

  3 O'tmishdagi ANIQ VAQTDA davom
    etayotgan ish:
    'James WAS SLEEPING at 9
     o'clock last night.'

  4 Hikoyada FON ma'lumoti:
    'The wind WAS BLOWING when Jane
     left work.'


⚠ 'WHILE' va 'WHEN':

  while + past continuous
  when + past simple


⚠ 'IN PROGRESS':

  = davom etayotgan.


⚠ 'TO INTERRUPT':

  = uzmoq, to'xtatmoq.


⚠ 'BACKGROUND':

  = fon.

points.en: We form the past continuous with was/were (past tense of the verb "to be") and add -ing to the base form of the main verb. I was eating, you were eating. I wasn't eating. Was I eating? Yes, I was. / No, I wasn't.
points.uz: O'tgan davomli zamonni was/were ('to be' fe'lining o'tgan zamoni) va asosiy fe'lga -ing qo'shib yasaymiz. I was eating, you were eating. I wasn't eating. Was I eating? Yes, I was. / No, I wasn't.

points.en: Two or more actions happening at the same time in the past. John was cutting the grass while Jenny was planting flowers.
points.uz: O'tmishda bir vaqtda bo'lgan ikki yoki undan ko'p ish. John o't o'rayotganda Jenny gul ekayotgan edi.

points.en: An action which was in progress when another action interrupted it. We use the past continuous for the action in progress (longer action) and the past simple for the action that interrupted it (shorter action). She was having a bath when the phone rang.
points.uz: Boshqa ish uzganida davom etayotgan ish. Davom etayotgan (uzunroq) ish uchun o'tgan davomli, uzgan (qisqaroq) ish uchun o'tgan oddiy zamon. U cho'milayotganda telefon jiringladi.

points.en: An action in progress at a stated time in the past. James was sleeping at 9 o'clock last night.
points.uz: O'tmishdagi aniq vaqtda davom etayotgan ish. James kecha soat 9 da uxlayotgan edi.

points.en: Background information in a story. The wind was blowing when Jane left work last Friday.
points.uz: Hikoyada fon ma'lumoti. O'tgan juma Jane ishdan chiqqanda shamol esayotgan edi.

exercises.instructionEn: Adverbs usually describe verbs. He drives fast. Form: We usually form adverbs by adding -ly to the adjective. careful - carefully. When the adjective ends with a consonant + y, we drop -y and add -ily. lucky - luckily. Some adverbs have the same form as their adjectives: hard, fast, early. Note: good → well.
exercises.instructionUz: Ravishlar odatda fe'llarni tasvirlaydi. U tez haydaydi. Shakli: Ravishlarni odatda sifatga -ly qo'shib yasaymiz. careful - carefully. Sifat undosh + y bilan tugasa, -y ni tashlab -ily qo'shamiz. lucky - luckily. Ba'zi ravishlar sifati bilan bir xil shaklda: hard, fast, early. Eslatma: good → well.
exercises.explanationUz:
RAVIShLAR (ADVERBS).

  Ravish FE'LNI tasvirlaydi
  (qanday?):
  'He drives FAST.' = U tez
  haydaydi.

  ⚠ Sifat OTNI tasvirlaydi:
  'a fast car' (sifat)
  'drives fast' (ravish)


ShAKLI:

  1 SIFAT + -LY:
    careful → carefully
    slow → slowly, quick → quickly
  2 undosh + y → -ILY:
    lucky → luckily
    happy → happily, easy → easily
  3 BIR XIL ShAKL:
    hard → hard (qattiq)
    fast → fast (tez)
    early → early (erta)
    late → late (kech)
  4 NOTO'G'RI:
    good → WELL
    'He is a good driver. He drives
     WELL.'


⚠ 'HARDLY' ≠ 'HARD':

  hard = qattiq; hardly = deyarli
  yo'q. 'He works hard' ≠ 'He
  hardly works'!

points.en: Adverbs usually describe verbs. He drives fast.
points.uz: Ravishlar odatda fe'llarni tasvirlaydi. U tez haydaydi.

points.en: We usually form adverbs by adding -ly to the adjective. careful - carefully
points.uz: Ravishlarni odatda sifatga -ly qo'shib yasaymiz. careful - carefully

points.en: When the adjective ends with a consonant + y, we drop -y and add -ily to form the adverb. lucky - luckily
points.uz: Sifat undosh + y bilan tugasa, -y ni tashlab -ily qo'shamiz. lucky - luckily

points.en: Some adverbs have the same form as their adjectives. hard → hard, fast → fast, early → early. Note: good → well
points.uz: Ba'zi ravishlar sifati bilan bir xil shaklda. hard → hard, fast → fast, early → early. Eslatma: good → well

patterns.formula: X is as + SIFAT + as Y.
patterns.exampleEn: My brother is as tall as my father.
patterns.exampleUz: Akam otam bilan bir xil bo'yda.

patterns.formula: X is much + SIFAT-ER than Y.
patterns.exampleEn: An elephant is much heavier than a mouse.

patterns.formula: X was + -ING when Y + PAST SIMPLE.
patterns.exampleEn: She was having a bath when the phone rang.
John was cutting the grass while Jenny was planting flowers.
patterns.exampleUz: John o't o'rayotganda Jenny gul ekayotgan edi.
